project_scope.selection_mode: All six already canonical; learner inclusion independent from county-native certification; revised visual pass 2026-10-13
project_scope.note: All six concepts are installed learner cards. Three locally PASS-labelled cards (affinis, lutea, tenuiloba); range HOLD on foetida/incarnata; TARGET_ZONE_FAIL on lanuginosa. Range decision is distinct from learner admission. Verify county evidence in separate audit.

study_strategy.warning: Do not identify Passiflora from flower color alone. San Antonio-area records are especially vulnerable to confusion between native P. foetida and introduced P. lanuginosa/ciliata-type plants; use leaf/bract/fruit morphology plus provenance.
study_strategy.look_here_first: Check a leaf margin (TOOTHED or ENTIRE), then the petiole for nectar glands. Next turn the leaf over for underside nectar dots (especially affinis vs lutea), and look under the flower for tiny bracts or a large sticky cage. Last compare flower/fruit size. Large purple maypop is easy, small yellow passionflowers are not.

quick_split: P. affinis — canonical PASS; broad cowboy-hat leaves, floral bracts present, greenish-yellow flower, purple-black berry.
P. lutea — canonical PASS; glandless petiole, broad rounded entire 3-lobed leaves, tiny green-yellow flower and small berry.
P. tenuiloba — canonical PASS; paired cuplike petiole glands and extremely narrow deeply divided birdwing leaves; tiny green petal-less-looking flower.
P. incarnata — reviewed range HOLD; paired petiole glands, large broad serrate 3-lobed leaves, enormous purple/white corona flower, large maypop fruit.
P. foetida — reviewed range HOLD; densely hairy fetid foliage, finely divided sticky bract cage, pale flower with purple-blue corona, greenish mature fruit.
P. lanuginosa — reviewed target-zone FAIL; introduced Mexico–Guatemala lookalike with darker angular leaves, pinker flowers, and smooth red fruit.

highest-value affinis vs lutea microscopic field cue

species_comparison_matrix.affinis: >25 mm, outer corona filaments >10 mm and clubbed/tipped
species_comparison_matrix.lutea: <25 mm, outer corona filaments <10 mm straight
species_comparison_matrix.lanuginosa: pinkish possible; never identify by color alone

species_comparison_matrix.foetida: Green to yellow-green in FNA Texas key; elsewhere P. foetida can ripen yellow or red, so color alone is not definitive
species_comparison_matrix.lanuginosa: Reddish, often smooth when mature in reviewed concept, but red fruit also occurs in nonlocal P. foetida
species_comparison_matrix.importance: Compare mature fruit with leaf hairs, bract shape, provenance, and accepted taxon concept; NEVER use red color alone

comparison_cards.title: Cowboy hat or yellow passionflower?
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Flip a mature leaf and inspect lower surface: affinis has nectar dots on the underside, lutea lacks them. Affinis has floral bracts + >25 mm flower with clubbed wavy corona tips; lutea has no floral bracts and smaller straighter filaments. BOTH lack petiole nectaries.
photo_roles: bracts vs no bracts under flower
comparison_cards.caution: Do NOT confuse underleaf nectaries with petiole glands: both affinis and lutea have EGlandular petioles.

comparison_cards.title: Birdwing or yellow?
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Tenuiloba has a pair of cuplike petiole glands and narrow deeply cut leaf lobes; lutea has no petiole glands and wider more rounded shallow lobes. Tenuiloba may have dramatically different leaves on ONE vine.
photo_roles: multiple leaves from one tenuiloba plant
comparison_cards.caution: Do not use a single unusual leaf silhouette to rule out tenuiloba.

comparison_cards.title: Fetid or scarletfruit?
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Inspect finely divided sticky bracts, stem/leaf hairiness, leaf lobes and mature fruit, then verify identity from the source taxon concept. FNA differentiates its Texas P. foetida as green/yellow-green-fruited from P. ciliata with red fruit, but other geographic P. foetida concepts can ALSO have red fruit. Smooth red fruit by itself does not certify P. lanuginosa.
comparison_cards.caution: Do not teach red fruit as a diagnostic guarantee of P. lanuginosa: published regional accounts document red P. foetida elsewhere. Use a full character combination, source geography and taxonomic reconciliation; avoid labeling introduced plants as Texas-native foetida.

comparison_cards.title: Maypop or birdwing?
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Both have petiole glands; incarnata has broad SERRATED lobes and a large showy corolla/corona with large fruit; tenuiloba has narrow mostly ENTIRE lobes, small greenish flowers with petals absent, and tiny dark berries.
